verdict.rationale: LiveKit ships its own isolated development mode: `livekit-server --dev` runs a local server with placeholder API credentials, and the CLI lets you talk to an agent locally before deploying to LiveKit Cloud. That gives a non-production test path, and a community user confirms the local dev server was easy to stand up. Nothing documents a dedicated sandbox environment or project, or any guarantee of separation from production data. missing for 10: an explicit sandbox/test environment or project in LiveKit Cloud, documented isolation of test data from production data, sandbox-specific credentials or limits, and independent corroboration beyond local dev mode.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Start LiveKit in development mode by running `livekit-server --dev`. It'll use a placeholder API key/secret pair.
Scaffold an agent, talk to it locally, and deploy it to LiveKit Cloud:
deploying a local dev server was easy
